## Satis Appraisal v0.2.4

A correctness release. No new features — five rounds of financial audit against the
model itself, and every defect found reproduced numerically before it was fixed. The
figures the app produces have changed in places, and each change is a case where the
old number was wrong.

### The appraisal no longer rewards a longer programme
- **Build cost now moves with tender prices.** House price inflation indexed sale prices
  forward to completion while the building contract stayed at today's money — on the demo
  scheme that manufactured **£386,876 of profit out of nothing but elapsed time**, and made
  a slower programme look *more* profitable. There is now a separate tender-price inflation
  input, researched alongside the sales figures and deliberately independent of HPI, because
  tender prices and house prices do not move together. It ships switched off, so no saved
  project changes on opening, and the app warns whenever HPI is indexing revenue with cost
  inflation left off.

### Each exit is now priced on the costs it actually incurs
- **Refinance-and-hold no longer pays to sell.** The hold scenario was charged the whole
  sales & marketing group — **£93,723 of agent fees on a sale that never happens**, plus
  sales legals — while carrying no letting costs at all. Every cost line now records which
  exits incur it, there is a new letting-cost group (tenant find, EPCs, inventory,
  licensing), and the hold is priced on its own cashflow. On the demo it now releases a
  **£144,899 surplus** where it previously showed a £2,049 shortfall.
- **Holding costs grow with the hold.** Council tax, insurance and utilities on unsold
  units were a fixed lump however long the sell-down ran: £13,550 whether it took 3 months
  or 24, while interest correctly scaled six times over. They are per-month figures now, so
  a 24-month hold costs eight times a 3-month one — which is the slow-sales case the
  scenario exists to test.

### Floor areas match the building
- **Irregular floors are no longer laid out on a rectangle.** L-, T- and U-shaped floors
  were planned across the full bounding box while the area was measured from the true
  outline, so units were placed in space the building does not occupy. A test floor
  reported **124% net-to-gross — physically impossible** — and overstated GDV by about a
  quarter. Units and rooms are now clipped to the real outline, and an appraisal cannot
  report more internal area than the floor contains.

### The workbook export matches the screen
- **Repaired inputs reach the workbook.** The app silently corrects fat-finger entries and
  tells you it has, but the Excel export was built from the *raw* figures — a mistyped 450%
  bridge rate reached the workbook while the screen and the audit strip showed the corrected
  50%.
- **Large schedules are no longer silently trimmed.** Exporting more than 30 units dropped
  the rest without a word: **£5,997,990 of GDV vanished** from a 42-unit test. The export
  now reports exactly what the workbook's sheets cannot carry.

### Degenerate inputs say so instead of showing a confident number
- **A cash-rich scheme no longer earns money by arranging a loan.** Where committed equity
  exceeded costs, the development facility estimate went negative and its arrangement fee
  became **finance income of -£12,191**, quietly reducing total costs.
- **Zero sales velocity is reported as no sales.** It used to read "sold out at completion,
  15 months" beside a loan that never repays and £1.16m of extra interest — two
  contradictory answers on one screen.
- **Months with no funding source are flagged.** Pre-construction spend above the bridge
  advance plus equity was money out with no source and no interest charged. It was detected
  every month and shown nowhere; it now names the months and the amount.
- **Ratios that cannot be calculated read "n/a", not zero.** A schedule with no sale prices
  used to **pass the loan-to-GDV covenant**, because the ratio defaulted to zero and zero is
  under the limit. Profit on cost, profit on GDV, interest cover and cash-on-cash behaved
  the same way. A real covenant breach still reads as a breach.
- **The refinance warns when rent does not cover the interest.** The demo's cover of 0.87 —
  £193,800 of net rent against £223,374 of interest — now says so plainly, rather than
  presenting an exit no lender would fund as a live option.

### Under the hood
The built-in financial audit grew from 48 to 61 checks, including a new class that asks
whether a figure *could be true of a real scheme* rather than only whether the model agrees
with itself — which is how several of the defects above went unnoticed. The test suite grew
from 145 to 251 tests.

Saved projects open unchanged: every behaviour that would move a stored figure ships off by
default, and that guarantee is pinned by tests. Figures remain **pre-tax** throughout — no
corporation tax on SPV profit, no VAT on works — and the exported assumptions now say so
rather than leaving it to be inferred.

**Full changelog**: https://github.com/Satisgroup-1/Appraisalapplication/compare/v0.2.3...v0.2.4
